title: すなわち — “namely / that is to say”
summary: A formal connecting word that restates or defines the previous item in other words: “namely, that is.” It comes right after a noun or clause and is followed by the equivalent expression. Mostly used in writing and formal speech.

patterns.form: 名詞A、すなわち 名詞B
patterns.gloss: A, namely B (B is another name or definition of A)
Sentence. That is, sentence (restates the previous sentence)

body.p: すなわち places two items on an equal footing: the second one is the same thing as the first, said more concretely or in another way. 日本の首都、すなわち東京. It is placed between two nouns with a comma, or at the start of a sentence.
It is typical of essays, news and explanations, where you define a term or give a precise number or name. In everyday conversation, つまり is much more common.
つまり can also draw a conclusion (“so, in short…”). すなわち is closer to a strict equation: A and B really are the same thing, such as 零度 and 氷点.

examples.ja: 日本（にほん）の首都（しゅと）、すなわち東京（とうきょう）はとても大（おお）きい。
examples.romaji: Nihon no shuto, sunawachi Tōkyō wa totemo ōkii.
examples.tr: Japan's capital, namely Tokyo, is very big.
examples.note: Tokyo is the concrete name of the capital.

examples.ja: この学校（がっこう）で一番（いちばん）長（なが）い人（ひと）、すなわち校長（こうちょう）が話（はな）した。
examples.romaji: Kono gakkō de ichiban nagai hito, sunawachi kōchō ga hanashita.
examples.tr: The person who has been at this school the longest, namely the principal, spoke.

examples.ja: 水（みず）は零度（れいど）、すなわち氷点（ひょうてん）で凍（こお）り始（はじ）める。
examples.romaji: Mizu wa reido, sunawachi hyōten de kōri hajimeru.
examples.tr: Water begins to freeze at zero degrees, that is, at the freezing point.
examples.note: Both words name the same temperature.

pitfalls: Use it only when B really equals A. For a conclusion or summary, use つまり instead.
It sounds stiff. In casual talk, say つまり or 要するに.
